rubric.reason: No private-symbol assertions, no call-count assertions unrelated to an AC's own observable, no leaked private method/field names in test titles, and no assertion of a property an AC does not require. Direct construction of googleConnections/oauthStates rows in test/oauth-callback.test.ts and test/google-routes.test.ts (mintNonce, seedConnection) is arrange-phase seeding through exported schema tables, not an assertion against implementation detail — there is no other way to place the callback in an already-consumed/expired-nonce precondition, since no API exists to do so.

test/oauth-callback.test.ts:95, :106, :114, :123, :135, :168, :181 assert only `expect(res.status).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(400)` with no upper bound. Only the first test in the file (line 81-82: `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(400)` + `toBeLessThan(500)`) pairs the lower bound with an upper one. PRD AC-2 requires the callback to answer '4xx' specifically for a refused state; an unbounded `>=400` assertion is satisfied equally by a 500 thrown from an unhandled exception in the route handler (a crash) as by a deliberate 4xx rejection. Since these tests exist specifically to prove the security-critical refusal path (zero-outbound-calls-before-validation, per the manifest's own 'three assertions that carry more weight' section), a test that cannot distinguish 'validated and refused' from 'crashed before validating' is trivially satisfiable and does not prove what its own describe block claims.

None of the four categorical signals fire. The client is never mocked as the SUT (fetch is the third-party boundary being faked, not the module under test). No interface/protocol exists for `fetch` that a concrete-type mock bypasses. No mock chain reaches even 2 levels, let alone 3. Every stubFetch/recorder-based test asserts on the recorded Request's url/method/body or on a downstream effect (connectionCount, taskCount, nonce state) rather than only `toHaveBeenCalled` — e.g. test/oauth-callback.test.ts:141-146 asserts outbound[0].url === the real token endpoint, not merely that fetch was invoked. The two-seam mixture (DI in test/google-client.test.ts vs vi.stubGlobal('fetch') in the two route suites) is justified and consistently applied per layer: `fetchMock` is confirmed absent from this project's pinned cloudflare:test (0.20.1, verified by the manifest empirically), DI is used exactly where a parameter can be threaded (the client module itself), and vi.stubGlobal is used exactly where the call travels through the real Hono app with no injection point — never the reverse. In every route-level rejection test, `outbound` is freshly emptied by stubFetch() in beforeEach (test/oauth-callback.test.ts:66-70, test/google-routes.test.ts:69-73) or explicitly re-emptied mid-test before the assertion that matters (test/oauth-callback.test.ts:163-165, `outbound = []` before the replay call) — no test relies on a stale array to pass its zero-calls assertion.

All five in-scope ACs have genuine, non-vacuous test references. AC-1: test/google-oauth.test.ts (URL/scope construction) + test/google-routes.test.ts 'POST /api/google/connect' (nonce persistence, freshness, no outbound call). AC-2: test/oauth-callback.test.ts 'the callback refuses every state it did not mint' (6 tests spanning never-minted/consumed/expired/missing-state/missing-code/error-redirect). AC-3: test/oauth-callback.test.ts 'a valid callback stores the credential exactly once' + test/google-client.test.ts exchangeCode tests. 'Exactly once' specifically is tested by the pairing of 'exchanges the code and stores the refresh token' (connectionCount()===1 after the first call, test/oauth-callback.test.ts:141-148) with 'makes a replay of the identical URL fail and change nothing' (connectionCount()===1 still, after a replay, test/oauth-callback.test.ts:159-171) — the replay-does-not-duplicate assertion is what makes 'exactly once' observable rather than merely 'stores'. AC-4: test/google-routes.test.ts 'DELETE /api/google/connection' (revoke call sent, credential deleted, N Task rows preserved via seedTasks(5), idempotent, 401-gated). AC-5: 'succeeds even when Google refuses' (non-2xx and thrown-network-error cases) + test/google-client.test.ts revokeToken non-2xx/network-error tests.

No pair of tests asserts the same observable property over inputs in the same equivalence class. The refusal-path tests in test/oauth-callback.test.ts each exercise a distinct equivalence class of isNonceUsable/route-validation (never-minted, already-consumed, expired, missing state, missing code, provider-error-redirect); the AC-5 tests in test/google-client.test.ts and test/google-routes.test.ts cover distinct failure modes (non-2xx vs thrown network error) rather than restating the same case with different literals.

Dynamic execution reproduced the manifest's claim: exit code 1 across all 4 suites. test/google-oauth.test.ts and test/google-routes.test.ts fail with 'Cannot find module ../src/shared/google-oauth'; test/google-client.test.ts fails with 'Cannot find module ../src/worker/google/client' — both unresolved modules are Task 4/Task 5 CREATE entries in the plan's Files to Change (seam set). test/oauth-callback.test.ts fails with a murkier signal, 'D1_ERROR: incomplete input' from `db.delete(googleConnections)` at line 68 — independently confirmed by grepping src/worker/db/schema.ts, which currently exports neither `googleConnections` nor `oauthStates` (both are Task 2 UPDATE entries in the seam set). The module import itself resolves (schema.ts exists) so Drizzle receives `undefined` for the table and builds a malformed `delete from` with no table name, producing a Drizzle/D1 error rather than a compile-time 'named export not found' error. Every unresolved symbol across all four suites is in the plan's seam set and none is a typo, wrong import path, or unrelated dependency — legitimate red-by-design, consistent with the manifest's own honest accounting of the murky failure.

Create-only session, verified independently via git rather than trusting the ledger's prose: `git status --porcelain` shows all four test files (test/google-oauth.test.ts, test/google-client.test.ts, test/oauth-callback.test.ts, test/google-routes.test.ts) as untracked (??), and `git log --diff-filter=A` over those paths returns no prior commit — none existed before this session. No UPDATE or DELETE op is present in the observed diff, so completeness check (a) and the (b)/(c)/(d) anti-weakening checks are vacuously satisfied; the ledger's table (four CREATE rows only) matches the observed diff exactly.
